title: Poker Machine Harm Reduction ($1 Bets and Other Measures) Bill 2012 [2013]
short_title: Poker Machine Harm Reduction ($1 Bets and Other Measures) Bill 2012 [2013]

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would set national restrictions on poker machine betting, payouts and credit loading, backed by civil penalties and a staged timetable for compliance.
It would cap each spin's total wager at $1 and each winning payout at $500, while preventing machines from accepting banknotes worth more than $20.
Operating restrictions would apply to venues with more than 10 machines from 1 January 2017, and smaller venues would have until 31 December 2018.
changes: From 1 January 2013, corporations could sell or lease only machines capable of operating within the proposed limits.
From 1 January 2017, corporations could sell or lease only machines complying with those limits.
Machines would reject additional credits whenever a player's existing balance was $20 or more.
Court-imposed civil penalties could reach 2,000 penalty units for each contravention.
The bill would also provide for uniform national harm minimisation standards effective from 1 January 2015 and a national poker machine monitoring network.
summary.affected: Corporations selling or leasing poker machines, licensed venues operating them, players, the responsible minister and the Federal Court are affected.
